chapter_title: Concept of Mole and Chemical Calculation

sections.content_markdown: Concept of Mole and Chemical Counting 113
**Individual Task:** Determine the number of $H$, $S$ and $O$ atoms in $1\text{ g H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

The volume that $1$ mole of a gaseous substance occupies is called the molar volume of that gas. $0^\circ\text{C}$ temperature and $1\text{ atm}$ pressure together is called the standard temperature and pressure or the standard condition. The volume of $1$ mole gas in this standard condition is $22.4\text{ liter}$.

If $n = \text{mole number}$
$w = \text{mass in gram}$
$V = \text{Volume in liter}$
$N = \text{Number of molecules}$
$M = \text{Molecular mass}$

$$n = \frac{w}{M}$$

$$\text{Or, } n = \frac{V}{22.4}$$

$$\text{Or, } n = \frac{N}{6.023 \times 10^{23}}$$

**Problem:** How many molecules are there in $1\text{ liter CO}_2$ gas at standard temperature and pressure?

**Solution:** $1\text{ mole CO}_2 = 44\text{ g CO}_2 = 6.023 \times 10^{23}\text{ no CO}_2\text{ molecules} = 22.4\text{ liter CO}_2\text{ gas at standard temperature and pressure}$

At standard temperature and pressure $22.4\text{ liter CO}_2\text{ gas contains} = 6.023 \times 10^{23}\text{ no CO}_2\text{ molecules}$

Therefore, $1\text{ liter CO}_2\text{ gas contains} = \frac{6.023 \times 10^{23}}{22.4} = 2.69 \times 10^{22}\text{ molecules}$
